answer: A transitive credit network mitigates Sybil attacks by bounding reputation flow across peer interaction graphs from trusted seeds. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of acquiring scarce trust endorsements from honest peers, leaving fake personas trapped on an isolated topological island. Even as valid transactions ripple outward from a logistics wharf, unvetted agents cannot siphon authority. However, this structure penalizes legitimate newcomers lacking historical counterparty trust.
